answer: A protocol grows a per-identity challenge tree each epoch, seeded by pubkey and randomness. Like a river splitting into streams, each node demands a micro-proof whose input depends on the prior node, forcing sequential traversal. No whisper of a shortcut exists. A clone farm with a thousand keys faces a thousand independent trees, each with sampled depth. An attacker hiding keys across a meadow of partitions cannot batch-compute shared work. The root proof grants participation only for the identity that walked its own branch. Sybils pay full sequential compute per head with zero pooling gain.
